standard.title: Noun groups and verb groups
standard.description: understand that in sentences nouns may be extended into noun groups using articles and adjectives, and verbs may be expressed as verb groups
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand the major word classes — nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs (AC9E1LA07). They have not yet examined how these elements combine into extended noun groups and verb groups that carry richer meaning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can understand how nouns are extended into noun groups through articles and adjectives, and how verbs are expressed as verb groups.

nodes.label: Extending a noun into a noun group
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that articles and adjectives extend a bare noun into a noun group that provides more specific information.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the noun, article and at least one adjective in a given noun group (e.g. 'the longest side').
nodes.typical_width: Identify noun groups in sentences from a range of texts, naming the head noun and the articles and adjectives that extend it; build extended noun groups from bare nouns by asking 'how many?', 'what type?', 'what's it like?'
wider: Compare noun groups across different text types — sparse noun groups in procedures vs rich noun groups in narratives — and discuss why each text type uses them differently
Build noun groups from bare nouns in cross-curriculum texts (e.g. 'the ancient Egyptian artefact') and discuss how each element adds information

response_modes.reason: Students often treat adjectives as decoration rather than as group-builders. Seeing noun groups across different text types — where some texts deliberately minimise them and others maximise them — helps students understand that noun group length is a purposeful choice, not random. More text-type examples is the productive move.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Building noun groups using the questioning scaffold ('how many?', 'what type?', 'what's it like?') is a genuinely generative technique that works across all subjects and text types. Advancing students can build increasingly complex noun groups and analyse their effects — real richness available here.
success_criteria: Student can identify the head noun and at least one extending element (article or adjective) in a noun group.
Student can build an extended noun group from a bare noun by adding at least an article and one adjective.

nodes.label: Verb groups
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that verbs can be expressed as verb groups — combining an auxiliary or modal verb with a main verb — and explain what the group adds over a simple verb.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify a verb group in a sentence (e.g. 'was touched', 'is running') and identify the main verb and its auxiliary.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and build verb groups using auxiliaries ('was', 'is', 'has been') and discuss how they change meaning — tense, aspect — compared to a simple verb.
wider: Compare active and passive verb groups ('touched' vs 'was touched') and discuss the effect on who or what is foregrounded
Identify verb groups in shared reading texts from different subject areas and discuss what the auxiliary adds
success_criteria: Student can identify the main verb and auxiliary in a verb group.
Student can explain one way the auxiliary changes the meaning of the verb (e.g. tense, passive voice).

nodes.label: Noun groups and verb groups in text
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify both noun groups and verb groups in sentences, and explain how they work together to create more precise and expressive sentences.
nodes.minimum_width: In a given sentence, identify the noun group and the verb group and name their key elements.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse sentences across several texts for noun group and verb group complexity; revise simple sentences by expanding noun groups and extending verb groups.
wider: Compare two versions of a sentence — one with simple nouns and verbs, one with extended groups — and discuss how the expanded version changes the image or meaning
Write a short descriptive paragraph deliberately using extended noun groups and verb groups, then annotate what was added and why

response_modes.reason: This node requires students to coordinate noun group and verb group knowledge simultaneously within sentences — the two concepts reinforce and interact. Coordinated identification and production is the learning demand.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The revision task — taking simple sentences and expanding noun and verb groups — is productively open-ended. Advancing students can explore how expanded groups change imagery, specificity and tone in ways that connect to their own writing development.
success_criteria: Student correctly identifies both the noun group and verb group in a given sentence.
Student can expand a simple sentence by extending at least its noun group or its verb group.
